set.approach: The Bookend Cliffs sit on the east ridge running off the American Fork Twins, on the south side of Mineral Basin above Snowbird. From the top of the tram at Hidden Peak, head for the white avalanche-mitigation mast; a bolted stance on the mast's left side marks the foot of an obvious arete, which is where the route begins.
set.descent_text: Rappelling the route straight down is discouraged because of a detached flake on the face. Instead the party tensions off to skier's right and drops into the steep scree couloir beside the cliff, which can hold snow and ice and needs careful footing.

review.notes: Route page gives the approach from Hidden Peak and the descent off to skier's right into the scree couloir; the page text of the descent is cut off so only that much is stated.

set.approach: Park on the large shoulder on the east side of the Little Cottonwood Canyon road, a short way beyond the Tanners Campground turnoff and before the bend. Across the road a trail starts behind the Tanners Slide Path highway sign; follow it (faint in places) to the drainage and walk up the gulch. The first pronounced gully on the left is Witches and Divas, and the east-facing Exceeded Expectations Wall stands on the right side of its mouth, with the shortest approach in the gulch. This is the far right route on the wall; the start is broken ground with loose dirt and rock. In winter and spring the gulch can slide, so check the avalanche forecast.
set.descent_text: Lower off the anchor, which has lower-offs.

review.notes: Route page: far right route, anchors have lower-offs; area pages: wall location and trail.

set.approach: From the Crystal Lake trailhead take the trail toward Wall Lake, cross the bridge over the outlet on its east side, and follow the well-defined trail up switchbacks above the lake to Hope Lake. Continue on the east side of Hope Lake up to the pass, go by Lake Lovenia, and descend switchbacks to Ibantik Lake. The route is on the northeast face of Notch Mountain: cross the talus along the foot of the wall, pass one chimney or alcove and go on to a second chimney, where a flat spot makes a place to rack up. Walk into the narrowing chimney to find the first belay.
set.descent_text: The route ends near the top of Notch Mountain, after a short scramble up a ramp and an easy fifth-class dihedral. From the summit, head west from the summit down to the Notch Mountain saddle, then follow cairns by the easiest line back to the Notch.

review.notes: Route page: northeast face start and summit walk-off; area page: trail from Crystal Lake trailhead to Ibantik Lake.

set.approach: Low Tide is approached from the top. Reach the cliff edge as for the Shattered Sea, then keep walking toward the Shattered Sea along the rim, where the trail skirts broken rock and short cliffs. When the ground drops away and opens up with less deadfall, look for cairns on the right near some pines marking the top of the crag, and go down a short, steep talus chute that is best handled with a rope. Better do Better climbs the right-hand arete where the left gap opens out.

review.notes: Area page: approach from the rim; route page: where the route starts. No descent stated for this route.

set.approach: Park at the Lower Jungle pullout, a flat rocky spot on the right of the road, and take the cairned trail that begins with a few big steps up and a built-up log crossing. The trail runs north along the foot of the cliff band through the Lower Jungle routes. Kaa is the short, steep wall between Dr. Livingstone, I Presume? and Man Next Door.

review.notes: Area page: parking and trail along the cliff band; route page: between two named routes.

set.approach: From the top station of the Needles gondola at Snowbasin, hike up the upper bike loop trail, turn right off it after a short way, and climb beyond a stand of conifers across the alpine meadow toward the lower part of the main slab. The route is on the right side of the main wall.
set.descent_text: Both pitches end on bolted belays, and from the second a short scramble reaches the ridgeline. To get down, rappel the route, taking care when pulling the ropes on the upper rappel because they can snag rocks.

review.notes: Route page: right side of main wall, rappel the route; area page: hike from the gondola top.

set.approach: The Lofty Lake trailhead, just beyond the Mirror Lake turnoff on the left when coming from Kamas, is the place to start. Take the Weber River Trail west and bear left at the metal sign at the fork. Further on, leave the trail to the left toward Reids Peak; there is no path from there, so choose the easiest line to the talus field below the wall and work up the talus to the base. Keep clear of the fragile meadows.
set.descent_text: The route finishes at steel lower-off carabiners; lower from them.

review.notes: Area page: trailhead and off-trail approach; route page: steel lower-off biners. The route page gives no start position.
